legend: Find the number of different strings of length k%%ZSMJ0%% that you can get by concatenating prefixes of a given string S%%ZSMJ1%%.
input: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line of input contains a single integer t%%ZSMJ2%% (1≤t≤2000%%ZSMJ3%%)  — the number of test cases. The description of test cases follows.
The first line contains two integers n%%ZSMJ4%% and k%%ZSMJ5%% (1≤n≤k≤2000%%ZSMJ6%%)  — the length of S%%ZSMJ7%% and the size of the desired strings.
The second line contains a string S%%ZSMJ8%% consisting of n%%ZSMJ9%% lowercase letters. It is guaranteed that the sum of k%%ZSMJ10%% over all test cases does not exceed 2000%%ZSMJ11%%.
output: For each test case, print a line with one integer  — the answer to the problem. Since the answer may be huge, print it modulo 998244353%%ZSMJ12%%.
